edges.limitations: The fly phenotype is maternal-effect, arising in the early embryo, which has no counterpart in a recessive human disorder caused by zygotic loss. The model is a null, whereas the recurrent human allele is missense. PMID:34905536 reports no fly phenotype corresponding to the human cardiac or renal malformations or to microcephaly, and does not examine the ER and mitochondrial findings of the human disease.

nodes.description: RNA sequencing of fibroblasts from the three p.Gly168Asp individuals against four parents found 21 differentially expressed genes, including extracellular matrix genes involved in the migration of neuronal precursors. This is a transcriptional signal in fibroblasts. It has not been shown in neural tissue, and the connection to the neurodevelopmental phenotype is the authors' interpretation rather than a tested step, so no edge to a phenotype is drawn.

nodes.description: TM2D3 binds Notch1 outside its ligand-binding domain and increases Notch1 at the cell surface, which is a prerequisite for ligand-induced endocytosis and activating cleavage. Tm2d3-null mouse embryonic fibroblasts show less full-length and S1-processed Notch1 and less surface Notch1 and Notch2. In Drosophila, loss of the orthologue almondex impairs endocytosis of the Notch extracellular domain and Delta in early embryos. None of this has been examined in patient cells.

nodes.description:
Biallelic TM2D3 variants, including the recurrent missense allele c.503G>A (p.Gly168Asp). TM2D3 is a transmembrane protein expressed in many tissues and most abundant in the central nervous system, and in SNB75 cells it localizes to the endoplasmic reticulum. Loss of function is inferred from the similarity of patient fibroblasts to TM2D3-knockout cells. The missense alleles may be hypomorphic rather than null; that distinction is not resolved in the abstract.
The bound molecular function, Notch binding, is the only activity shown experimentally for TM2D3: the wild-type protein physically associates with Notch1. That the disease alleles reduce it is inferred from the node, not measured. GO's other function annotation for TM2D3, G protein-coupled receptor activity, rests on phylogenetic inference alone and is not bound.
